library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Stepniewska_2009_artesunate"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1186/1475-2875-8-200>
* Open-access full text: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3224946/>

Stepniewska 2009 compared a then-new fixed-dose combination (FDC) of
artesunate (AS) and amodiaquine (AQ) with the same two drugs given as separate
("loose") tablets, in children aged 6 months to 5 years with uncomplicated
*Plasmodium falciparum* malaria in Burkina Faso. Both regimens were given once
daily for three days. The paper fits three independent population PK models,
each packaged here as its own model file:

| Model file | Analyte | Structure |
|---|---|---|
| `Stepniewska_2009_amodiaquine` | desethylamodiaquine (DeAQ) after AQ dosing | 2-compartment, first-order appearance (ka fixed) |
| `Stepniewska_2009_artesunate` | dihydroartemisinin (DHA) after AS dosing | 1-compartment, first-order absorption |
| `Stepniewska_2009_artesunate_activity` | total anti-malarial activity (AS + DHA, molar sum in DHA equivalents) | 1-compartment, first-order absorption |

Amodiaquine itself was "usually low or not detectable" and was not modelled;
artesunate on its own was not modelled either, but enters the total-activity
model. All three models were fitted in S-PLUS 6.0 following the approach of
Simpson 2006 (`modellib("Simpson_2006_artesunate")`), with clearances and
volumes expressed per kilogram of body weight.

# Population

140 children were randomised (64 female, 76 male; median age 32 months, range
7-59 months). The first 70 formed the artesunate PK group and the next 70 the
amodiaquine PK group, 35 per arm in each (Table 1). Seven children who vomited
within an hour of dosing were excluded (four AS, three AQ), as were two AQ-group
children with detectable AQ before the first dose.

```{r population}
pop_tbl <- function(name) {
  p <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(name))$population
  tibble::tibble(
    Model = name,
    Field = names(p),
    Value = vapply(p, function(x) paste(x, collapse = "; "), character(1))
  )
}
dplyr::bind_rows(
  pop_tbl("Stepniewska_2009_amodiaquine"),
  pop_tbl("Stepniewska_2009_artesunate")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(Field %in% c("n_subjects", "n_subjects_pk", "age_range", "weight_range", "sex_female_pct", "dose_range", "sampling")) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Population metadata (Stepniewska 2009 Table 1 and Methods).")
```

Sampling was sparse. The AS group gave a pre-dose sample and one sample at
0.5, 1, 2 or 4 h (randomised) after the first and the third dose. The AQ group
gave a pre-dose sample, a sample 4 h after the third dose, one on Day 7 or 14 and
one on Day 21 or 28.

```{r load-models}
mod_aq <- readModelDb("Stepniewska_2009_amodiaquine")
mod_dha <- readModelDb("Stepniewska_2009_artesunate")
mod_act <- readModelDb("Stepniewska_2009_artesunate_activity")
ui_aq <- rxode2::rxode(mod_aq)
ui_dha <- rxode2::rxode(mod_dha)
ui_act <- rxode2::rxode(mod_act)
```

# Check 1: typical values reproduce the published identities

The paper prints neither the covariate equations nor the centring of the age
effect, but it does print derived quantities that pin them down: typical
half-lives (Table 3 and Table 4) and AUCs, computed in the paper as
dose / CL/F for a 3.7 mg/kg artesunate dose and a 34 mg/kg total amodiaquine
dose (Results). The checks below solve the packaged models with the random
effects zeroed for a 32-month-old, 12-kg child, so both sides use the same
parameters and the tolerance only has to absorb the paper's rounding.

```{r typical}
typ_child <- data.frame(WT = 12, AGE = 32 / 12)

typ_1cmt <- function(ui) {
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(0, 24, 48), amt = 3.7 * 12, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 72, by = 0.05), amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(MULTI_DOSE = as.integer(time >= 24), WT = 12, AGE = 32 / 12)
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), events = ev, returnType = "data.frame")
}
s_dha <- typ_1cmt(ui_dha)
s_act <- typ_1cmt(ui_act)

# AUC by trapezoid over each 24-h interval: the drug is gone well before the
# next dose (half-lives of 1-2.5 h), so this is the single-dose AUC0-inf.
auc_int <- function(s, from, to) {
  x <- s[s$time >= from & s$time <= to, ]
  sum(diff(x$time) * (head(x$Cc, -1) + tail(x$Cc, -1)) / 2) / 1000
}
thalf <- function(s, t0) log(2) / s$kel[s$time == t0 + 1][1]

s_aq <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(ui_aq),
  events = rxode2::et(time = 0, amt = 1, cmt = "depot") |> rxode2::et(1, cmt = "central"),
  params = typ_child, returnType = "data.frame"
)
k10 <- s_aq$kel[1]
k12 <- s_aq$k12[1]
k21 <- s_aq$k21[1]
beta <- ((k10 + k12 + k21) - sqrt((k10 + k12 + k21)^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
thalf_aq_days <- log(2) / beta / 24
cl_aq_kg <- s_aq$cl[1] / 12

claims <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Claim, ~Source, ~Published, ~Packaged, ~Pass,
  # The published 9.0 days is the median of individual posterior predictions
  # (range 7.3-11.6), not the typical value, so it carries posterior shrinkage
  # as well as rounding.
  "DeAQ terminal half-life (days)", "Table 3 (median prediction)", "9.0", sprintf("%.2f", thalf_aq_days),
  abs(thalf_aq_days - 9.0) < 0.2,
  "DeAQ AUC for 34 mg/kg (ug*h/mL)", "Results", "57.76 / 54.75 by arm", sprintf("%.2f", 34 / cl_aq_kg),
  34 / cl_aq_kg > 54.75 * 0.98 && 34 / cl_aq_kg < 57.76 * 1.02,
  "DHA half-life, dose 1 (h)", "Table 4", "2.5", sprintf("%.2f", thalf(s_dha, 0)),
  abs(thalf(s_dha, 0) - 2.5) < 0.05,
  "DHA half-life, dose 3 (h)", "Table 4", "1.1", sprintf("%.2f", thalf(s_dha, 48)),
  abs(thalf(s_dha, 48) - 1.1) < 0.05,
  "DHA AUC, dose 1 (ug*h/mL)", "Results", "4.29", sprintf("%.2f", auc_int(s_dha, 0, 24)),
  abs(auc_int(s_dha, 0, 24) / 4.29 - 1) < 0.02,
  "DHA AUC, dose 3 (ug*h/mL)", "Results", "1.96", sprintf("%.2f", auc_int(s_dha, 48, 72)),
  abs(auc_int(s_dha, 48, 72) / 1.96 - 1) < 0.02,
  "Activity half-life, dose 1 (h)", "Table 4", "2.4", sprintf("%.2f", thalf(s_act, 0)),
  abs(thalf(s_act, 0) - 2.4) < 0.05,
  "Activity half-life, dose 3 (h)", "Table 4", "1.2", sprintf("%.2f", thalf(s_act, 48)),
  abs(thalf(s_act, 48) - 1.2) < 0.05,
  "Activity AUC, dose 1 (ug*h/mL)", "Results", "4.43", sprintf("%.2f", auc_int(s_act, 0, 24)),
  abs(auc_int(s_act, 0, 24) / 4.43 - 1) < 0.02,
  "Activity AUC, dose 3 (ug*h/mL)", "Results", "2.14", sprintf("%.2f", auc_int(s_act, 48, 72)),
  abs(auc_int(s_act, 48, 72) / 2.14 - 1) < 0.02
)
knitr::kable(claims, caption = "Published typical-value claims against the packaged models.")
stopifnot(all(claims$Pass))
```

Two structural readings rest on these numbers:

* **The dosing-period effect on CL/F is additive.** 0.636 + 0.760 = 1.396
  L/kg/h gives the third-dose AUC (2.742 / 1.396 = 1.96) and half-life (1.1 h)
  exactly. A proportional reading (0.636 x 1.760) would give 2.45 ug*h/mL and
  1.4 h.
* **The dose was converted to DHA on a molar basis.** 3.7 mg/kg of artesunate
  is 3.7 x 284.9 / 384.4 = 2.742 mg/kg of DHA, and 2.742 / 0.636 = 4.31, against
  the published 4.29. Without the conversion the AUC would be 5.82.

# Check 2: the age effect reproduces the published half-life range

Table 4 prints the 90% range of the predicted DHA half-life as 0.8-4.5 h after
the first dose and 0.4-2.0 h after the third. Clearance has no random effect,
so this spread comes entirely from V/F, i.e. from the age effect and the 47%
IIV. The packaged form, V/F = 2.285 + 0.063 x (age in months - 32), spans
0.71-4.0 L/kg over the 7-59-month age range on its own, which already
reproduces the published range; an exponential form per month would span
27-fold and a per-year form would leave almost no age effect at all.

```{r age-range}
ages <- seq(7, 59, by = 1)
vkg <- 2.285 + 0.063 * (ages - 32)
tibble::tibble(
  `Dose period` = c("Dose 1", "Dose 3"),
  `Published 90% range (h)` = c("0.8-4.5", "0.4-2.0"),
  `Age effect alone, 7-59 months (h)` = c(
    sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", min(log(2) * vkg / 0.636), max(log(2) * vkg / 0.636)),
    sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", min(log(2) * vkg / 1.396), max(log(2) * vkg / 1.396))
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "DHA half-life spread from the age term alone.")
```

The individual predictions behind the published range are posterior
estimates from at most two samples per child, so they are shrunk towards the
typical value; the full population simulation below, which carries the whole
IIV, is correspondingly wider.

# Virtual cohort

Each model gets 150 children per arm. Age is drawn uniformly over the
published 7-59-month range; weight is the WHO median weight-for-age scaled by
0.92 to match the Table 1 medians (12-14 kg) with 10% log-normal scatter,
truncated to the published 6-31 kg range. Doses follow the age bands of the
trial: the FDC tablet held 25 mg AS / 67.5 mg AQ (one tablet below 12 months,
two from 12 months), and the loose regimen used 50 mg AS and 153 mg AQ tablets
(half a tablet of each below 12 months, one from 12 months).

```{r cohort}
# rxSetSeed() fixes rxode2's stream for a given thread count only; set.seed()
# fixes R's RNG for the covariate draws. Neither makes the cohort identical
# across machines, so every assertion below is on centres and robust quantiles.
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20090820)
set.seed(20090820)

who_age <- c(6, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60)
who_wt <- c(7.6, 9.3, 11.8, 13.9, 15.8, 17.9)
n_arm <- 150L

make_children <- function(arm, offset) {
  age_mo <- stats::runif(n_arm, 7, 59)
  wt <- 0.92 * stats::approx(who_age, who_wt, xout = age_mo)$y * exp(stats::rnorm(n_arm, 0, 0.1))
  wt <- pmin(pmax(wt, 6), 31)
  young <- age_mo < 12
  # Both regimens give 25 mg AS below 12 months and 50 mg from 12 months; AQ
  # differs (FDC 67.5 / 135 mg, loose 76.5 / 153 mg).
  as_dose <- ifelse(young, 25, 50)
  aq_dose <- if (arm == "FDC") ifelse(young, 67.5, 135) else ifelse(young, 76.5, 153)
  tibble::tibble(
    id = offset + seq_len(n_arm),
    arm = arm,
    AGE = age_mo / 12,
    WT = wt,
    as_mg = as_dose,
    aq_mg = aq_dose
  )
}
kids <- dplyr::bind_rows(make_children("FDC", 0L), make_children("Loose", 1000L))

kids |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    N = dplyr::n(),
    `Median age (months)` = stats::median(AGE * 12),
    `Median WT (kg)` = stats::median(WT),
    `Median AS (mg/kg/day)` = stats::median(as_mg / WT),
    `Median AQ (mg/kg/day)` = stats::median(aq_mg / WT),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = arm) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Virtual cohort (compare Table 1; target doses 4 mg/kg/day AS, 10 mg/kg/day AQ).")
```

# Simulation: DHA and total anti-malarial activity

`MULTI_DOSE` switches from 0 to 1 at the second dose. The paper sampled only
after doses 1 and 3, so the clearance during the second dosing interval is not
identified by the data; the model gives it the later-dose value.

```{r sim-dha}
dose_times <- c(0, 24, 48)
obs_1cmt <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 6, by = 0.25), seq(7, 24, by = 1), 48 + seq(0, 6, by = 0.25), 48 + seq(7, 24, by = 1))))

ev_as <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tidyr::crossing(kids, time = dose_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = as_mg, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  tidyr::crossing(kids, time = obs_1cmt) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(MULTI_DOSE = as.integer(time >= 24)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, arm, WT, AGE, MULTI_DOSE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

sim_dha <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_dha, events = ev_as, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")
sim_act <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_act, events = ev_as, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_dha$Cc), !anyNA(sim_act$Cc))
```

```{r vpc-dha, fig.cap = "Simulated DHA and total-activity concentrations after the first and third dose (median and 5th-95th percentile by arm). Compare the observed DHA concentrations of Figure 3 (mostly 100-3,600 ng/mL within 4 h)."}
vpc_1cmt <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_dha |> dplyr::mutate(analyte = "DHA"),
  sim_act |> dplyr::mutate(analyte = "Total activity (DHA eq)")
) |>
  dplyr::filter((time > 0 & time <= 6) | (time > 48 & time <= 54)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    period = ifelse(time < 24, "First dose", "Third dose"),
    tad = ifelse(time < 24, time, time - 48)
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(analyte, arm, period, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = stats::median(Cc), Q95 = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc_1cmt, aes(tad, Q50, colour = arm, fill = arm)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(analyte ~ period) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)", colour = "Arm", fill = "Arm") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Simulation: desethylamodiaquine

```{r sim-aq}
obs_aq <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 72, by = 1), seq(78, 672, by = 6), seq(696, 1344, by = 24))))
ev_aq <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tidyr::crossing(kids, time = dose_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = aq_mg, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  tidyr::crossing(kids, time = obs_aq) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, arm, WT) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

sim_aq <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_aq, events = ev_aq, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_aq$Cc))
```

```{r vpc-aq, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5 of Stepniewska 2009: predicted DeAQ concentrations over the first 14 days by arm (median and 5th-95th percentile)."}
sim_aq |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0, time <= 336) |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = stats::median(Cc), Q95 = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "DeAQ concentration (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

The simulated profiles peak at roughly 300-600 ng/mL a few hours after the third
dose and fall below 100 ng/mL by Day 7, as in Figure 5.

## DeAQ concentrations against Table 2

Table 2 reports the median measured DeAQ concentration at each sampling visit.
The simulated median at the same nominal times is shown beside it. The
measured medians come from 10-32 children per cell and include children who
carried DeAQ from an earlier amodiaquine course (pre-dose median 8-9 ng/mL),
which the model does not represent.

```{r table2}
table2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~visit, ~time, ~Loose, ~FDC,
  "4 h after dose 3", 52, 396.6, 347.1,
  "Day 7", 168, 73.9, 91.5,
  "Day 14", 336, 48.8, 41.0,
  "Day 21", 504, 29.0, 17.7,
  "Day 28", 672, 17.7, 17.4
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Loose, FDC), names_to = "arm", values_to = "observed")

cmp_t2 <- sim_aq |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% table2$time) |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(simulated = stats::median(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(table2, by = c("arm", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = simulated / observed)

cmp_t2 |>
  dplyr::select(visit, arm, observed, simulated, ratio) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Visit" = visit, "Arm" = arm, "Table 2 median (ng/mL)" = observed,
    "Simulated median (ng/mL)" = simulated, "Simulated / observed" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median DeAQ concentration by visit and arm.")

# Structural: a mis-transcribed clearance or volume shifts every visit by tens
# of percent. Envelope on the median ratio only, not on any single cell.
stopifnot(nrow(cmp_t2) == 10L, abs(log(stats::median(cmp_t2$ratio))) < log(1.3))
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports exposure as AUC = dose / CL/F from the posterior clearances:
for DeAQ, normalised to a total amodiaquine dose of 34 mg/kg and also for the
dose actually received; for DHA and total activity, normalised to a 3.7 mg/kg
artesunate dose after the first and the third dose. The PKNCA runs below
reproduce those scenarios: the normalised ones with every child dosed at exactly
the reference mg/kg, the actual-dose one with the cohort above. The AUCs are
printed in ng*h/mL by the paper but are numerically in ug*h/mL (see
Assumptions); they are compared here in ug*h/mL.

```{r pknca-aq}
nca_aq <- function(events) {
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_aq, events = events, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")
  conc <- sim |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, arm, time, Cc)
  conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(conc, conc |> dplyr::distinct(id, arm) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)) |>
    dplyr::distinct(id, arm, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time)
  dose <- events |>
    dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
    dplyr::select(id, arm, time, amt)
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | arm + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | arm + id),
    intervals = intervals
  ))
  as.data.frame(res) |>
    dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(PPORRES = ifelse(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs", PPORRES / 1000, PPORRES / 24))
}

ev_aq_norm <- ev_aq |> dplyr::mutate(amt = ifelse(evid == 1L, 34 / 3 * WT, amt))
nca_aq_norm <- nca_aq(ev_aq_norm) |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "34 mg/kg (normalised)")
nca_aq_act <- nca_aq(ev_aq) |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "Actual dose")

ref_aq <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~arm, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life,
  "34 mg/kg (normalised)", "Loose", 57.76, 9.0,
  "34 mg/kg (normalised)", "FDC", 54.75, 9.0,
  "Actual dose", "Loose", 62.5, 9.0,
  "Actual dose", "FDC", 48.7, 9.0
)
cmp_aq <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = dplyr::bind_rows(nca_aq_norm, nca_aq_act),
  reference = ref_aq,
  by = c("scenario", "arm"),
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "ug*h/mL", half.life = "day")
)
knitr::kable(cmp_aq, caption = "DeAQ: simulated median AUC0-inf and terminal half-life against Stepniewska 2009 (Results, Table 3). * differs by >20%.")
```

```{r pknca-aq-gate}
med_auc_norm <- stats::median(nca_aq_norm$PPORRES[nca_aq_norm$PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"])
med_thalf <- stats::median(nca_aq_norm$PPORRES[nca_aq_norm$PPTESTCD == "half.life"], na.rm = TRUE)
# 34 / 0.61 = 55.7 for the typical child; the published arm medians bracket it.
stopifnot(abs(med_auc_norm / 55.7 - 1) < 0.08, abs(med_thalf / 9.0 - 1) < 0.15)
```

The normalised AUC and the terminal half-life agree with the published values
in both arms. The actual-dose AUCs also agree: the label age bands give the
loose arm about 9% more amodiaquine per kilogram than the FDC arm in the virtual
cohort, in line with the "approximately 10% higher" dose the paper reports for
the loose arm. Because CL/F carries the only random effect and is the same
distribution in both arms, the arm-to-arm difference in the normalised scenario
is sampling noise between two sets of 150 children.

```{r pknca-dha}
nca_1cmt <- function(mod, analyte) {
  ev <- ev_as |> dplyr::mutate(amt = ifelse(evid == 1L, 3.7 * WT, amt))
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")
  conc <- sim |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, arm, time, Cc)
  conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(conc, conc |> dplyr::distinct(id, arm) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)) |>
    dplyr::distinct(id, arm, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time)
  dose <- ev |>
    dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
    dplyr::select(id, arm, time, amt)
  intervals <- data.frame(
    start = c(0, 48), end = c(24, 72),
    cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
  )
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | arm + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | arm + id),
    intervals = intervals
  ))
  as.data.frame(res) |>
    dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life", "cmax", "tmax")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      analyte = analyte,
      period = ifelse(start == 0, "Dose 1", "Dose 3"),
      PPORRES = ifelse(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs", PPORRES / 1000, PPORRES)
    )
}
nca_dha <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nca_1cmt(mod_dha, "DHA"),
  nca_1cmt(mod_act, "Total activity")
)

ref_1cmt <- tibble::tribble(
  ~analyte, ~period, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life,
  "DHA", "Dose 1", 4.29, 2.5,
  "DHA", "Dose 3", 1.96, 1.1,
  "Total activity", "Dose 1", 4.43, 2.4,
  "Total activity", "Dose 3", 2.14, 1.2
)
cmp_1cmt <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_dha |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life")),
  reference = ref_1cmt,
  by = c("analyte", "period"),
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "ug*h/mL", half.life = "h")
)
knitr::kable(cmp_1cmt, caption = "DHA and total activity after a 3.7 mg/kg artesunate dose: simulated median AUC0-inf and half-life against Stepniewska 2009 (Results, Table 4). * differs by >20%.")
```

```{r pknca-dha-gate}
gate_1cmt <- nca_dha |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(analyte, period, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim = stats::median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    ref_1cmt |> tidyr::pivot_longer(c(aucinf.obs, half.life), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("analyte", "period", "PPTESTCD")
  )
stopifnot(nrow(gate_1cmt) == 8L)
# CL/F has no random effect, so AUC is the same for every child up to the
# integration; the half-life medians carry the V/F spread.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(gate_1cmt$sim[gate_1cmt$PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"] / gate_1cmt$ref[gate_1cmt$PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"] - 1) < 0.03),
  all(abs(gate_1cmt$sim[gate_1cmt$PPTESTCD == "half.life"] / gate_1cmt$ref[gate_1cmt$PPTESTCD == "half.life"] - 1) < 0.15)
)
```

```{r pknca-dha-cmax}
nca_dha |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(analyte, period, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = stats::median(PPORRES), p05 = stats::quantile(PPORRES, 0.05), p95 = stats::quantile(PPORRES, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename("Analyte" = analyte, "Dose period" = period, "Parameter" = PPTESTCD, "Median" = median, "5th pct" = p05, "95th pct" = p95) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated Cmax (ng/mL) and Tmax (h) after a 3.7 mg/kg artesunate dose. The paper reports no NCA Cmax; Figure 3 shows observed DHA up to about 3,600 ng/mL after dose 1 and 2,700 ng/mL after dose 3.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Age effect on V/F.** Table 4 gives "Effect of Age on V/F" = 0.063 without an
  equation, units or centring value. The packaged form is additive on the
  per-kilogram V/F, per month of age (the unit the paper uses throughout),
  centred at the median age of the randomised cohort (32 months):
  V/F = 2.285 + 0.063 x (age - 32). It matches the published typical half-lives
  (Check 1), which require V/F at the typical child to equal the tabulated
  value, and the published half-life range (Check 2). It also follows the
  additive per-kilogram covariate convention of Simpson 2006, which the paper
  cites for its method. The same form is used for the total-activity model.
  The model takes `AGE` in years, as elsewhere in the library, and converts it
  to months internally.
- **Dosing-period effect on CL/F.** Additive on the per-kilogram CL/F, as
  confirmed by the third-dose AUCs and half-lives (Check 1). The paper's
  covariate was 0 for samples after dose 1 and 1 for samples after dose 3; the
  library's `MULTI_DOSE` indicator is used, and the second dosing interval,
  which was not sampled, takes the later-dose value.
- **AUC units.** The Results print the AUCs in "ng/mL.h", but the values equal
  dose (mg/kg) / CL/F (L/kg/h), which is in mg*h/L, i.e. ug*h/mL. They are
  compared in ug*h/mL here.
- **DeAQ dose is the amodiaquine base dose without molar correction.** The
  normalised AUC (34 mg/kg / 0.61 L/kg/h = 55.7 ug*h/mL against published arm
  medians of 57.76 and 54.75) shows no amodiaquine-to-DeAQ molecular-weight
  conversion was applied, so CL/F and V/F are in amodiaquine-dose terms.
- **Pre-treatment DeAQ is not modelled.** 28 children had DeAQ but no AQ before
  the first dose. The paper modelled those levels as first-order elimination of
  an earlier dose subtracted from the study profile; that component has no
  published parameters and is not part of the packaged model.
- **IIV and residual SDs.** The paper defines the reported CV% as the square root
  of the variance estimate, so the variances are the squared CVs. The DeAQ sigma
  is on the natural-log scale (`lnorm`); the DHA and total-activity sigmas are
  additive in ng/mL.
- **Covariates screened but not retained** (temperature, respiratory rate, sex,
  log parasitaemia, gametocytaemia, formulation; and age for DeAQ) are listed
  in each model's `covariatesDataExcluded`.
- **Cohort construction.** Age is uniform over the published range, and weight
  is a scaled WHO median weight-for-age with 10% scatter, because the paper
  gives only medians and ranges. Doses follow the label age bands. The cohort
  characterises the model; it does not reproduce the estimation data set.
- **No erratum** or correction is indexed for this article in Europe PMC
  (checked 2026-11-19).
- **No parameter was tuned.** Every `ini()` value is the published Table 3 or
  Table 4 value.
